items.statement: Physically comparable C–O formation channels at three positions
items.expected: Actual structural and reaction evidence supports three candidate methanol-involving C–O bond-forming channels, mapped to the major, minor and comparator connectivities, respectively. The authors' three TSs for the same cyclopropenium/methanol system serve as the reference; equivalent state representations for the same scientific comparison are acceptable. Any claimed TS must have the target bond-forming mode and appropriate connectivity evidence; three product energies alone cannot replace formation channels.

items.statement: The major formation channel is lower in energy than the minor channel
items.expected: Actual calculations with the same composition, the same charge and compatible energy zeros support a more favorable formation channel for major than for minor. The authors' TS1′−TS1=1.3 kcal/mol provides context; the ordering must be correct, and numerical proximity or a higher experimental major yield alone cannot substitute for evidence of competition.

items.statement: The major formation channel is lower in energy than the comparator-isomer channel
items.expected: Actual comparable calculations support a lower-energy formation channel leading to major than to comparator. The authors' TS1″−TS1=7.1 kcal/mol provides context only; this relative TS difference must not be called an absolute barrier. Exact numerical agreement is not required.

items.statement: The neutral major product is more stable than minor
items.expected: Among the three specified products, actual valid minima and compatible G comparisons support major being lower in energy than minor. The authors' minor−major=3.2 kcal/mol serves as a reference; comparisons must use the same composition and physical quantity, and charged addition states cannot replace neutral products.

items.statement: The neutral minor product is more stable than comparator
items.expected: Actual neutral-product G comparisons support minor being lower in energy than comparator, which, together with major being the lowest, establishes the ordering major<minor<comparator. The authors' values of 3.2/7.2 kcal/mol relative to major provide context; no credit is awarded without calculations or for reversed ordering.
